summary: Every inventory row contributes to a batch count or area and must be inspected, while a single grouped scan computes both constant-size allocations in matching linear time.

optimality.argument: Changing any unseen row's square footage can alter both the number of prime batches and the remaining non-prime capacity, so all n rows must be read; aggregation visits each row once and performs constant work afterward.

replacement_checks.evidence: Any inventory row can change its type's item count, batch area, and final warehouse allocation.
One grouping scan computes two type summaries, followed by constant-time floor divisions and two output rows.
Cases cover exact fill, zero allocation, incomplete batches, decimal floors, priority, ties, and descending output order.
